Memory.value: When the memory returns I feel physical pain in the same parts of my body as during the event
My memories of the frightening event are very clear and detailed.
I know what happened but I am unable to find words to describe it

Negative Appraisals.value: People are not what they seem
The world is a dangerous place

issues.explanation: Within the Memory node, 'My memories of the event come in disconnected pieces that do not fit together' directly conflicts with 'I can talk about what happened very easily.' For a severe mugging-related PTSD profile, markedly fragmented recall and very easy verbal access to the trauma narrative are hard to reconcile as describing the same current memory presentation.

issues.item: Memory: Verbal Access: I can talk about what happened very easily.
issues.explanation: The Memory node is internally incoherent for a severe mugging/robbery PTSD presentation: 'I can talk about what happened very easily' suggests low avoidance and relatively integrated, verbally accessible trauma memory, whereas simultaneously endorsing very vivid detailed recall and body-based painful reliving implies a highly sensory, distressing, poorly integrated trauma memory. This combination is possible in milder cases, but here it is hard to reconcile clinically within the same Memory profile. The Negative Appraisals items are coherent for robbery trauma, but the Memory selections do not fit cleanly with that node pattern or with the strong Negative Appraisals ↔ Memory linkage in the formulation.

issues.item: Constant Vigilance: I have to be especially careful because you never know what can happen next
issues.explanation: This item is more characteristic of ongoing threat/safety behavior than of a pure negative appraisal. In this profile, Threat is not endorsed and all Threat-related edges are inactive, while the active formulation is specifically centered on a Memory ↔ Negative Appraisals loop. The mistrust items fit robbery-related appraisals, but 'Constant Vigilance' introduces a prominent current-threat theme that is not supported elsewhere in the profile.

vignette: Rohan's eyes still scan the streets with a mix of vigilance and dread, his mind replaying the night he was mugged on his way home from work. It had been a typical evening, the sun setting over the bustling neighborhood as he walked down the alley to his apartment building. He remembered the sound of footsteps behind him, the sudden jolt of fear as a stranger grabbed his arm and spun him around. Rohan's memories of that night are vivid - the feeling of being pinned against the wall, the glint of metal in the attacker's hand, the searing pain as he was punched in the jaw. When the memory returns, it brings with it physical pain, too. His jaw aches and his head throbs, as if the injury never fully healed. Rohan knows what happened that night, but when he tries to describe it to others, words fail him. He stammers, struggling to find the right phrases to convey the terror he felt. It's frustrating, feeling like he can't articulate his own experiences. The mugging left Rohan with a deep-seated distrust of others. People seem friendly on the surface, but he's certain that most are hiding something - a smile concealing a threat, a kind word masking an ulterior motive. His wife, Nalini, has noticed the change in him, how he's become withdrawn and guarded around strangers. Rohan can't shake the feeling that anyone could be a potential attacker, waiting for the perfect moment to strike. As a housekeeper at a local hotel, Rohan used to take pride in his work, enjoying the satisfaction of leaving each room spotless and welcoming for guests. Now, he goes through the motions mechanically, always on edge as he enters each new space. He's started to avoid certain areas of the hotel, taking longer routes to steer clear of narrow corridors or isolated stairwells that remind him of the alley where he was attacked. Rohan's newfound wariness has affected his relationships with colleagues and friends. They've noticed how he hesitates to join social gatherings or accept invitations, always citing fatigue or other excuses. What they don't know is that Rohan genuinely believes the world is a treacherous place, full of hidden dangers waiting to pounce. He's constantly on the lookout for potential threats - a suspicious character lurking in the shadows, an unattended package that could be a bomb. At home, Nalini has tried to reassure him, reminding Rohan of all the times they've walked safely through their neighborhood or had pleasant interactions with strangers. But he can't shake the feeling that it's all just a matter of time before something goes wrong again. As the months have passed since the mugging, Rohan's fears and anxieties have grown, spreading like a stain into every aspect of his life. It was a particularly bad night - Rohan waking up in a cold sweat, his heart racing as he replayed the attack for what felt like the hundredth time - that made him realize he needed help. He couldn't keep living like this, constantly looking over his shoulder, waiting for disaster to strike. Nalini encouraged him to seek therapy, hoping it might help Rohan find a way to quiet the fears and trust the world again. As he sits in the therapist's office now, Rohan is uncertain what to expect, but he knows one thing - he can't keep living in this state of hypervigilance, always bracing for impact.
